screened.motion: This house believes a team that cannot show the return on its AI coding spend should cut it.
screened.why: Both reject a blanket "cut it" rule because teams have never proven ROI on IDEs or CI either, and both would cap runaway or fast-growing spend rather than cut the tool itself.

screened.motion: This house believes every release of a widely used package should need a second maintainer's approval before it publishes.
screened.why: Both agree that stolen tokens beat approvals and that hardware keys, repo pinning and cooldowns matter more, but Claude still backs second approval as a default for high-download packages if it uses strong authentication, while Gemini rejects the mandate as bureaucracy that burns out solo maintainers.

motion: This house believes every release of a widely used package should need a second maintainer's approval before it publishes.
why: Editor's check: In its closing, Claude says that in LiteLLM a stolen token published "alone" by one actor, as a single-account hijack, but the brief says the attackers used stolen tokens from three engineers.
alt: The Motion, Motion 9. This house believes every release of a widely used package should need a second maintainer's approval before it publishes. Claude, after arguing for, alone: "On the motion as written, every release needing a second maintainer, I'd probably vote no."
